claim_text: pCloud says a cyberattack targeted its pCloud Pass password manager and was promptly contained
summary: pCloud says a cyberattack targeted pCloud Pass, its password manager, and that its team promptly contained it.
detail: pCloud gave the statement in reply to customers' posts on Reddit; BleepingComputer (Nov 27) and The Hacker News (Nov 28) each reported it, with their own reporting on what customers saw. pCloud has not published a notice on its own website.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: BleepingComputer, Nov 27, quoting pCloud: "A cyberattack targeting pCloud Pass occurred, which was promptly contained by the pCloud team." The Hacker News, Nov 28, quotes the same statement.
notes: Both outlets quote one pCloud statement posted on Reddit; each also reported separately on what customers saw.

claim_text: pCloud says a small number of pCloud Pass users' email addresses were exposed and login attempts were made
summary: pCloud says a small number of pCloud Pass users' email addresses were exposed and that login attempts were made, and that it automatically sent a notification to each of those addresses.
detail: pCloud has not said how many addresses were exposed.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: BleepingComputer and The Hacker News both quote pCloud: "Unfortunately, a small number of pCloud Pass user email addresses were exposed and login attempts were made. Our system sends a notification automatically to each of these addresses."

claim_text: pCloud says passwords, notes and other information stored in pCloud Pass were not compromised, because they are encrypted and need the Master Password
summary: pCloud says the passwords, notes and other information stored in pCloud Pass were not compromised, because they are encrypted and can only be opened with the user's Master Password.
detail: This is the company's account. It has not said whether attackers reached or copied the encrypted vaults themselves (see c007).
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BleepingComputer, Nov 27: pCloud says "passwords, notes, and other information stored in pCloud Pass have not been compromised." The Hacker News: stored information is "encrypted and can only be accessed after providing a Master Password."
notes: The company's word alone; nobody outside has checked it.

claim_text: pCloud says the incident was limited to pCloud Pass and its cloud storage was not affected
summary: pCloud says the incident was limited to pCloud Pass and that pCloud's cloud storage service was not affected.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Hacker News, Nov 28: pCloud "said the incident was limited to pCloud Pass, and that pCloud Cloud Storage services are not affected." BleepingComputer reports the same.

claim_text: Customers reported emails saying a new device had connected to their pCloud Pass accounts
summary: Customers in several countries reported emails telling them a new device had connected to their pCloud Pass account, some of them with two-factor authentication turned on.
detail: Customers described an unfamiliar device named "pd", which users said connected from an address in Luxembourg belonging to pCloud's own network. Some found no unfamiliar device when they checked their account.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: BleepingComputer: customers "received email notifications that a new device had connected to their pCloud Pass accounts", some "despite having two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled". The Hacker News reports the same alerts.
notes: Both outlets read the customers' posts; this says what customers reported, not how the attackers got in.

claim_text: Some people who never used pCloud Pass also received the new-device alert
summary: Some people who said they had never used pCloud Pass also received the new-device alert, one at an address tied to a pCloud storage account they had asked to delete almost a year earlier.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BleepingComputer: some users said they received alerts despite never using the password manager, one at "an email address associated with a pCloud storage account they had requested be deleted almost a year ago."
notes: One outlet; pCloud has not addressed it.

claim_text: pCloud has not said how the attackers got in, when, whether any login succeeded, or whether encrypted vaults were taken
summary: pCloud has not said how the attackers got in, when the intrusion happened, whether any of the login attempts succeeded, or whether any encrypted vaults were accessed or copied.
detail: No attacker or group has been named.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Hacker News: "it's unclear if the sign-in 'attempts' were successful and if the attackers managed to access or download the encrypted vaults. pCloud also has not disclosed how the attackers got in".

claim_text: The alert's settings link pointed to a pCloud test (QA) address
summary: A link in the new-device alert pointed to a pCloud web address that appears to be an internal test (QA) environment, which did not load for those who tried it.
detail: BleepingComputer says it confirmed this in a copy of the alert shared with it. What it means has not been explained by pCloud.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BleepingComputer: the alert's "Open settings" link went to a hostname that appears to be a QA environment, and it "confirmed the link pointed there in a copy of the notification shared with it."
notes: Both rest on the same customer report; BleepingComputer checked a copy.

claim_text: pCloud warns users it will never ask for their Master Password or recovery words by email
summary: pCloud warns users to watch for phishing and says it will never ask for their Master Password or recovery words by email, phone or chat.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: BleepingComputer: pCloud warned it "will never ask for their master passwords or recovery words over email, phone, or chat." The Hacker News: pCloud "urged users to stay alert for phishing attacks".

claim_text: pCloud's statement says AI is speeding up the discovery of software flaws, but does not say AI was used in this attack
summary: pCloud's statement says AI is helping people find flaws in common software faster than before, but it does not say this attack used AI or a particular flaw.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Hacker News quotes pCloud: "With the advancement of AI, vulnerabilities in the software that every online service relies upon ... are being discovered faster than ever". BleepingComputer: not said to be AI-powered.

claim_text: pCloud is a Swiss-based cloud storage company that says it has over 24 million users; pCloud Pass is its password manager
summary: pCloud is a cloud storage company, run by pCloud International AG and described as Swiss-based, that says it has over 24 million users. pCloud Pass is its password manager for keeping passwords and filling them in on any device.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: pCloud About page: "Back in 2013, we set out to create something better" and "over 24 million users". Pass page: "pCloud Pass helps you keep your passwords". Wikipedia: "a Swiss-based cloud storage provider".
